subject: DPA: Role delegation and region-based routing questions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-03 09:12 -0700
Subject: DPA draft and a couple of routing/roles questions

Maria — attaching our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_Draft_v3.docx) and the SCCs annex for your review. A few items we want to flag up front so we can avoid back-and-forth later: 

- Role delegation: we’ve proposed Redwood as Processor for customer data, with Controller-level obligations retained by CloudHealth in section 2.3. There’s a note where telemetry/usage analytics that help improve the service is treated as Controller-collected under certain processing; see Exhibit B. Can you confirm if that approach matches your expectations?

- Region routing: CloudHealth earlier asked about EU-only routing for EU customers. We have a proposed fallback in the SCCs Annex where we commit to EU-only processing for customer-designated EU datasets when feasible; operationally we offer a routing/region control and an addendum for strict residency (addendum to the Order Form). Need to know whether CloudHealth will require strict residency or if the routing controls + SCCs annex are acceptable.

- Subprocessors: attached subprocessor_matrix.csv is our current list. Can you share CloudHealth’s approved vendor checklist and whether you require independent attestations (SOC2) for each subprocessors we list?

If helpful we can put a short 30-min sync on the calendar for legal + ops to walk the items. Aim: agree scope of DPA redlines and the evidence package we need to produce this week.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben — thanks for the packet, and for surfacing the three areas. Quick answers from my side and I’ve looped in our in-house counsel (legal@cloudhealth.com) for the formal redlines.

- Role delegation: Our privacy team needs to confirm whether the telemetry carve-out is acceptable. On principle we treat telemetry used to improve a vendor’s ML models as Processor activities, but we sometimes require explicit Controller approval for secondary uses.

- Region routing: For our EU customers we usually require either EU-only processing or a documented transfer impact/addendum showing compensating safeguards. We’ll confirm in writing; legal will send any stricter asks as part of their redlines.

- Subprocessors: please include a primary contact and last-audit date in the subprocessor_matrix.csv (we need last SOC2 or equivalent). Also flag any subprocessors located in APAC — our procurement team has a separate review track for those.

We expect to have initial redlines from legal by end of Friday local time. If Redwood can provide the latest SOC2 report and an operations contact for routing questions, that will speed things up.

—Maria

Maria / CloudHealth legal — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Redwood legal / privacy so we can align our redlines with yours: 

Summary positions (high level)
- Primary position: Redwood is Processor for customer data processed on behalf of CloudHealth.
- Exception: telemetry and aggregated usage signals used to improve the service are noted in Exhibit B; where CloudHealth reasonably objects, those items will be treated as Controller-authorized processing only with explicit instruction.

Open asks and attachments we’re including:
- Please confirm whether CloudHealth requires strict EU-only residency (i.e., an Order Form addendum specifying EU region physical processing) or if an SCCs Annex + region-routing contractual commitment is sufficient. If strict residency is required, we’ll need an explicit exhibit and capacity planning (we may need dedicated region pools).
- Subprocessor evidence: we will add last-audit-dates and primary contact columns to the subprocessor_matrix.csv and upload the latest SOC2 snapshot to the secure drive link. Please tell us the minimum acceptable attestations (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001) and whether self-attestations are allowed for niche tooling.
- SCCs changes: we propose the standard EU SCCs + minimal tailoring: (i) role mapping in clause 3.1; (ii) routing control language in clause 4.2; (iii) a transfer-impact addendum (TIA) as Exhibit D. If CloudHealth proposes additional tailoring, please provide redline suggestions.

Next steps / timeline
- Redwood legal (me) will draft an initial tracked-redline of the DPA and the SCCs Annex by Thursday EOD.
- Ops (Sofia) will produce region-routing runbook and the list of regions where processing can be constrained by Order Form.
- If CloudHealth requests EU-only residency we’d like to schedule a capacity call (ops + procurement) to scope dedicated resources.

Attachment: Redwood_open_questions_for_CloudHealth.docx (list of specific clause questions)

Laura / team — attached are CloudHealth’s standard DPA redlines and a short note on routing. Two items we want to highlight up front: 

1) EU-only processing ask: For our regulated EU clients, we require either (a) a contractual warranty that processing for EU-designated datasets will occur only in EU data centers, or (b) a TIA with technical and organizational measures plus the option for a dedicated EU processing addendum on the Order Form. We have provided both options in the redline so we can negotiate.

2) Subprocessor evidence: We require SOC2 Type II for any subprocessor that processes customer data in production environments. For monitoring/tooling (non-customer PII) we will accept ISO27001 or recent penetration test evidence.

We’ve uploaded our redlines: CloudHealth_DPA_Redlines_20260505.docx (attachment stub). Please review clause 4.2 (routing) and clause 7.1 (subprocessor approval) and propose alternative language if your standard is incompatible.

Links: Vendor Risk Portal: https://vendors.cloudhealth.com/portal/Redwood (procurement will upload the reviewed subprocessor list there).

Thanks — legal will be available for a 30-min sync tomorrow afternoon to walk clauses if that helps.

—CloudHealth Legal
